items.title: [Bug]: HF3FS metadata server never frees pages; every save fails once the page pool is used up
items.body:
`hf3fs_metadata_server.py` gives each rank a fixed free-page list (`hf3fs_file_size` / bytes per page). Pages return to the list only for failed writes, for keys that are already complete, or through `POST /clear` (which also removes the rank tables). There is no eviction, so the pool only shrinks. Also, `allocate_pages` returns nothing when fewer free pages remain than a save task needs, so near the end even small saves fail.

Observed with vLLM 0.31.0 (same code on `main`), Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, TP4, two instances sharing one metadata server, `hf3fs_file_size` = 64 GiB → 13,107 pages of 5 MiB (64 tokens) per rank, about 838,848 tokens: after about 25 minutes of tests, every save failed (`Page allocation failed`; the server logged `Rank N only allocated 0 pages for 128 keys`), 172 failed save tasks in 6 minutes and none successful, until we called `/clear` and registered the ranks again.

A bounded policy (for example LRU over complete keys, with the page returned to the free list and the key removed) or an eviction call from the connector would make the server usable as a long-running cache.

items.title: [Feature]: HF3FSKVConnector: support models with more than one KV cache shape (e.g. MLA + DSA indexer)
items.body:
With `GLM-5.3-NVFP4` (architecture `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`; TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64`, vLLM 0.31.0), the workers stop at start-up in `register_kv_caches` → `_setup_kv_cache_config`:
`AssertionError: HF3FS requires uniform KV cache shapes and strides.`
(`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/hf3fs/hf3fs_connector.py`, lines 548–551; the same check is on `main` and in v0.32.0.)
The model has a DSA indexer in addition to the MLA attention, so most probably the layers' KV caches have two different shapes (MLA latent cache and indexer key cache); we did not print the shapes. We expect DeepSeek-V3.2-style models to hit the same check. With the same model, `MooncakeStoreConnector` works.
Is support for more than one shape planned (for example, one page layout or file region per distinct shape)? Until then, a clear error at configuration time that names the unsupported model type would help.

items.title: [Bug]: HF3FSKVConnector ignores hf3fs_metadata_server_url (both metadata clients use localhost:18000)
items.body:
`HF3FSKVConnector` reads `hf3fs_metadata_server_url` from `kv_connector_extra_config` into `self._metadata_server_url`, but creates both metadata clients with `Hf3fsMetadataClient()` (no argument):

- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/hf3fs/hf3fs_connector.py` line 511 (scheduler side) and line 598 (worker side) on `main` (`38127f62`); the same in v0.31.0 and v0.32.0.
- The client default is `http://localhost:18000` (`hf3fs_metadata_server.py`, `Hf3fsGlobalMetadataClient.__init__`).

So the configured URL is never used. With the metadata server in its own pod/service (shared by several vLLM instances), each TP worker fails at start-up in `initialize` with `[Errno 111] Connection refused` to `localhost:18000`, then `RuntimeError: Failed to connect to metadata server`, and the engine does not start.

**Environment:** vLLM 0.31.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`), Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, TP4, two instances on two hosts, shared 3FS mount, `hf3fs_metadata_server.py` as a separate service.

**Fix** (2 lines):

```diff
-            self._metadata_client = Hf3fsMetadataClient()
+            self._metadata_client = Hf3fsMetadataClient(self._metadata_server_url)
```

in both places. With this change, all 4 ranks of both instances registered on the shared server, and instance B's first request for a prompt that instance A had computed (28,105 tokens) took 1.07–1.11 s (3 trials) against 2.37–2.39 s to compute it; 28,096 tokens came from the connector; the output was the same as on A.

I can open a PR with this change and a unit test (`Hf3fsMetadataClient` mocked, assert it is called with the configured URL).

items.title: [Performance]: Whisper log-mel runs on the renderer thread instead of the GPU worker
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

Whisper publishes `input_features` (`whisper.py`, about line 780). `embed_multimodal` forwards them into `get_encoder_outputs` (about lines 1003–1007). The renderer runs that processor on `_mm_executor` with `max_workers=1` (`renderers/base.py`, about lines 148 and 937).

Read at `9c778e9ff8d0c78a241d7f530c441c2dc1d67533`. Still present on main `e0adacc9a67a5f2b2d8ba508f7f522bc1ff83c6d` (2026-10-18).

`WhisperFeatureExtractor` builds log-mel with `_torch_extract_fbank_features` at `device="cpu"`, inside the renderer's single multimodal thread, under `set_default_torch_num_threads()` (`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, or else 1). `_postprocess_output` then casts that float tensor to the model dtype. The worker receives log-mel and starts at `conv1`.

The log-mel already matches the extractor to about `1e-5`. This moves that same STFT onto the GPU worker. Whisper only.

The STT pool (`VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_PREPROCESS_WORKERS`) only decodes and chunks. Its default is `min(cpu_count, 2)`, and the env var can already raise it. That pool leaves the STFT where it is. Voxtral already runs its own STFT on the worker and stays unchanged.

**Proposed change.** Same commit: ship float32 PCM, salt the processor-cache key, and run the extractor formula on the worker. API servers and Whisper workers roll onto that commit together.

1. `WhisperMultiModalProcessor` stops calling the Hugging Face extractor. The resampled mono waveform becomes passthrough `audio_pcm`: CPU float32, `batched("audio")`, `keep_on_cpu` left false. The processor stops publishing `input_features`.
2. `audio_pcm` stays out of the `BatchFeature` that `call_hf_processor` post-processes. `_postprocess_output` runs only there (`context.py` 437 and 447). `_finalize_hf_mm_data` merges passthrough afterward (`processor.py` 1312) and leaves the PCM out of that cast. A later edit that routes the field through `_postprocess_output` exempts it in that same commit.
3. Prompt length stays `WhisperProcessingInfo.get_num_audio_tokens()` == `max_source_positions`. `get_num_audio_tokens(duration)` stays the streaming usage counter only. It is not the placeholder length.
4. Salt `audio_ipc_schema="whisper_pcm_f32_v1"` into Whisper hash factors only, on a copy the extractor does not see. With no UUID, the hash is model id + resampled PCM + kwargs, including that key. With a UUID, `get_mm_hashes` hashes the UUID string plus those factors, not the PCM bytes (`inputs.py` 91–94). The key makes `has_hash_factors` true, so a bare UUID misses an unsalted entry.
5. The rollout that ships the commit clears unsalted entries: `clear_mm_cache`, `_mm_processor_only_cache`, worker `encoder_cache`, and EC `cross_encoder_cache` embeddings stored without that key.
6. `WhisperForConditionalGeneration.embed_multimodal` runs the formula below in float32 on `conv1.weight.device`, then casts to `conv1.weight.dtype`, then calls `get_encoder_outputs`. `WhisperEncoder.forward` stays `gelu(conv1)` then `gelu(conv2)`. A batch that still has log-mel `input_features` and no `audio_pcm` raises.

The STFT lives in `embed_multimodal`, not in `WhisperEncoder.forward`. `UltravoxWhisperEncoder.forward` replaces that method, skips `super()`, and still expects mel.

Per clip, constants from the loaded extractor:

1. Pad with `padding_value` or truncate to `n_samples = chunk_length * sampling_rate`. `do_normalize` stays off.
2. Hann window of length `n_fft` on the conv device.
3. Dither (`std = dither`) only when `extractor.dither != 0`.
4. `torch.stft(waveform, n_fft, hop_length, window=window, return_complex=True)`. The call keeps the extractor defaults for `center`, `pad_mode`, `win_length`, `normalized`, and `onesided`. `center=True` stays.
5. `magnitudes = (stft[..., :-1].abs() ** 2).contiguous()`. This is transformers 5.16.1 and 5.19.0. `.contiguous()` leaves the values unchanged.
6. Slaney mel filters, `1 + n_fft // 2` bins, 0–8000 Hz. `mel_spec = filters.T @ magnitudes`.
7. `clamp(min=1e-10).log10()`, then per-clip max−8 (max over time, then over bins, per row). Each clip has its own max.
8. `(log_spec + 4) / 4`, then cast to `conv1.weight.dtype`.

Mel time is `n_samples // hop_length` (stock 3000), so conv2 yields `max_source_positions` (stock 1500). Compare GPU STFT to CPU `_torch_extract_fbank_features` at about `1e-5`. GPU `torch.stft` matches within that tolerance and is not bit-identical. `torch.stft` stays eager, outside any encoder CUDA graph.

`return_attention_mask` hop-strides only `attention_mask`. It leaves `input_features` uncut. Whisper never reads that mask. Stock 480000 is divisible by hop 160, so the extra mask drop is unused.

Out of scope for this change:

- Raising `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_PREPROCESS_WORKERS`, `renderer_num_workers`, `_mm_executor`, or OMP threads. `set_torch_threads_for_runtime` wraps other calls. It returns without changing the count when `OMP_NUM_THREADS` was set outside vLLM.
- `mm_processor_kwargs["device"]="cuda"`. An accelerator processor is rejected unless the instance is encode-only, and it would still run STFT in the API process.
- Qwen2-Audio, Qwen3-ASR, Ultravox, GLM-ASR, and Moss. They share the placement and have different prompt math. Moss per-clip tokens come from `audio_data_seqlens` (`mel.shape[-1]` and `conv3_downsample_len`). `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item` is the 30-second hop ceiling, not the clip's mel length.
- Voxtral. Its STFT is already on the worker.

### Report of performance regression

None. Outputs stay within about `1e-5` of the CPU extractor. The move is off the renderer's single multimodal thread and onto the GPU worker.

### Misc discussion on performance

The worker already owns the encoder. The STFT is the piece still stuck on `_mm_executor` (`max_workers=1`). Shipping PCM instead of log-mel is what makes that move possible without changing prompt length.

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Source read on the commits above, against transformers 5.16.1 and 5.19.0. No full `collect_env.py` run. The `1e-5` figure is the existing extractor agreement, not a new GPU measurement.

### Checks

- Short, exact-`n_samples`, and over-long clips match CPU `_torch_extract_fbank_features` at about `1e-5`. Shared noise when dither is nonzero. Two clips in one batch each match their own max.
- `WhisperMultiModalProcessor` leaves `WhisperFeatureExtractor.__call__` unused. `audio_pcm` stays float32 through the passthrough merge.
- The schema key changes the no-UUID hash. A UUID hash is the UUID plus the factors, and it misses a bare-UUID entry. Replaying an unsalted log-mel entry leaves `audio_pcm` empty.
- Log-mel `input_features` with no `audio_pcm` raises in `embed_multimodal`.
- Ultravox still gelu-convs mel and still raises `Make sure to pad the input mel`.
- A 1 s clip and a 30 s clip both produce an encoder prompt of length `max_source_positions`.

items.title: [Performance]: Batch Whisper's conv stem and CUDA-graph only the fixed full-chunk mel
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

`WhisperEncoder.forward` loops `for features in input_features` and runs `gelu(conv1)` / `gelu(conv2)` once per item (`vllm/model_executor/models/whisper.py`, about lines 566–573). Read at `9c778e9ff8d0c78a241d7f530c441c2dc1d67533`. Still present on main `e0adacc9a67a5f2b2d8ba508f7f522bc1ff83c6d` (2026-10-18).

The conv modules are already the stock non-causal pair (`kernel_size=3`, `padding=1`, conv2 `stride=2`). Equal-length full chunks already match up to tolerance. The Python loop is a launch-per-item cost. A CUDA graph is valid only for the fixed full-chunk mel, because the encoder has no key-padding mask and the manager pads batch dimension 0, not time.

Related, and separate: #30549 (compile the encoder) and #59558 (tower LoRA).

**Batched stem on `WhisperEncoder`.**

Move the stem into `_conv_embed`: `gelu(conv1)`, `gelu(conv2)`, transpose, add `embed_positions.weight[:T]`, then `.to(embeds.dtype)`. Same parameters. The stem stays the stock conv: no `F.pad`, and no causal conv. The layer loop still passes `cu_seqlens=None`.

`forward`:

- Rank-3 tensor, including batch 1: one `_conv_embed` on the whole tensor.
- List of rank-3 tensors with equal shapes: `cat` on dim 0, then one `_conv_embed`. A list of one rank-3 tensor is the Moss call (`moss_transcribe_diarize.py`). That path is `cat`, not `stack`.
- List of rank-2 tensors with equal shapes: `stack`, then one `_conv_embed`.
- A bare rank-2 tensor, or unequal lengths: the current per-item loop.

`static_full_chunk_mel_frames()` returns `None` unless conv1 stride is 1, conv2 stride is 2, and both are kernel 3 with padding 1. Otherwise `mel_len = max_source_positions * conv2.stride`, and only if `(mel_len - 1) // 2 + 1 == max_source_positions`. Stock Whisper: 1500 → 3000. The 3000 falls out of that formula.

fp32 CPU: `B=1` rank-3 is `torch.equal` to the rank-2 stem. `B>1` matches within `1e-5` (max abs about `2e-7`) and is not `torch.equal`.

**CUDA graph only on `WhisperForConditionalGeneration`.**

Add `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` only on this class. Kimi still picks up the batched stem because it calls `WhisperEncoder.forward` and does not override it. Ultravox, MiniCPM, and Moss stay off the protocol. The protocol stays off `WhisperEncoder` itself, so Ultravox's `forward` override stays a plain eager encoder.

Two new interface methods default to `True` on `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph`, so existing Gemma4 and MiniCPM-O 2.6 image/video graphs stay:

```python
def encoder_cudagraph_capture_allowed(self) -> bool: ...
def should_use_encoder_cudagraph(self, mm_kwargs) -> bool: ...
```

The manager calls `get_encoder_cudagraph_config`, `get_encoder_cudagraph_budget_range(vllm_config)` with no `max_model_len` clamp, `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs`, `encoder_cudagraph_forward(..., path=)`, `get_encoder_cudagraph_item_specs`, `select_encoder_cudagraph_items`, `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_replay_buffers`, and `encoder_eager_forward(..., path=)`. It leaves `get_input_modality` and `get_max_frames_per_video` unused. `postprocess` / `scatter_output_slices` stay as they are.

Gemma4 modalities stay image/video. `_MiniCPMVEncoderCudaGraphMixin` stays as it is. `MiniCPMV4_5` / `MiniCPMO4_5` stay off the mixin. `MiniCPMV2_6` / `MiniCPMO2_6` stay on it for image/video.

Budget is `(max_source_positions, max_num_batched_tokens)`, not `max_model_len`. Whisper's `max_model_len` is `max_target_positions`, often 448. Clamping with it makes `min_budget=1500 > max_budget=448` and the manager raises (`encoder_cudagraph.py` 138–142).

Capture width for a budget is `n = min(token_budget // max_source_positions, max_batch_size)`. Raise if `n < 1`. Default `max_num_batched_tokens` is 2048, so auto budgets are `[1500, 2048]` and `max_batch_size = min(2048 // 1500, 1500) = 1`. Each default graph holds one full clip. The 2048 graph is an unused width-1 duplicate, because `round_up` selects 1500. Two clips need `max_num_batched_tokens >= 3000`.

`output_tokens` is `max_source_positions`, not 3000. `out_hidden_size` is `d_model` on the flat `(tokens, d_model)` layout. Capture is allowed only when `lora_config` is unset, the static mel length is known, and the FP8 scale path is present whenever `mm_encoder_attn_dtype == "fp8"`. The manager is still created only when `cudagraph_mm_encoder` is true (v2 also requires `not enforce_eager`).

Replay only when `input_features` is `(B, num_mel_bins, mel_len)` with `mel_len` equal to that static length. `mel_len - 1` has the same conv length and still declines: conv2's last window on odd `T` reads one past the end, an implicit zero. Right-padding the mel replaces that zero with a real frame, nonzero even when both biases are 0 (last-frame abs diff > `1e-3`). Captured `T` is that static full chunk. The mel is not time-padded.

`_copy_padded_buffer` is `dst.zero_(); dst[:src.shape[0]].copy_(src)`. It pads dim 0 only. A wider graph therefore replays a zero-mel suffix row. That row is a separate sequence because `cu_seqlens` stays `None`. The encoder layers see `(B, T, D)`. Scatter uses `output_tokens` and drops the suffix. The replayed forward runs the captured width. The live batch is sliced after replay, by the scatter.

`execute` returns `None` only when graphs were not captured or `should_use` is false. Both runners already fall back to `embed_multimodal`. `assert graph_output is not None` stays. A missing budget graph stays a hard failure for vision. It is not an eager fallback.

The captured region is `_conv_embed` plus the layer stack, not the Python per-item loop. With budgets `[8, 16]` and max items 2, budget 8 is width 1 and budget 16 is width 2.

### Report of performance regression

None. Equal-length full chunks already match the per-item stem up to tolerance. The change removes a launch per item and captures only the fixed full-chunk shape.

### Misc discussion on performance

Short clips and any mel length other than the static full chunk stay eager. The graph pads batch, never time, so a short clip cannot share a graph with a 30 s clip without changing the last conv frame.

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Source read on the commits above. The numeric notes (fp32 `B>1` max abs about `2e-7`, odd-`T` last-frame abs diff > `1e-3`) are from comparing the stock conv to a time-padded conv, not from a full `collect_env.py` run.

### Checks

New `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper_encoder_cudagraph.py`. Tiny local config: `max_source_positions=8`, so the static mel length is 16. No checkpoint download.

- `(1, n_mels, 16)` is `torch.equal` to the old per-item stem. `B>1` is `allclose` at `1e-5`, not `torch.equal`.
- `T=15` stays at 15. Zero both biases, compare against a pad to 16, and the last frame still differs by more than `1e-3`.
- `forward([rank-3])` matches `forward(rank-3)`. That is cat, not stack.
- CUDA: budgets `[8, 16]`, one clip selects budget 8, width 1, no suffix. Two clips select 16, width 2, no suffix.
- Suffix case uses its own manager with budgets `[16]` only, so one clip replays width 2 with one zero-mel suffix and still matches eager item 0. With `[8, 16]`, one clip hits 8 and has no suffix.
- Mel time 15: `execute` returns `None`.
- LoRA set, dynamic FP8, or a non-stock conv stem: capture stays off and `is_captured()` stays false.

items.title: [Bug]: FunASR merges 80 adaptor frames where the prompt length is 10; Cohere, FireRed, and Granite still build full conformer scores
items.body:
### Your current environment

Read at `9c778e9ff8d0c78a241d7f530c441c2dc1d67533`. Still present on main `e0adacc9a67a5f2b2d8ba508f7f522bc1ff83c6d` (2026-10-18).

No `collect_env.py` output. The FunASR mismatch is visible from the length formulas. The score cost is the full `T×T` matrix each encoder builds.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Four separate encoders. There is no shared attention module. Closed #54569 is an fp16 FunASR result report and is a different bug.

**FunASR adaptor length (wrong prompt).** `funasr.py` sets adaptor `olens = (ilens - 1) // k + 1` and, separately, prompt `fake_token_lengths`. For `L = 80` and `k = 1` those are 80 and 10. The LLM merge uses `olens`. The prompt was built for 10 tokens, so the merge and the prompt disagree.

**Full conformer scores (memory).**

- Cohere (`cohere_asr.py`) builds the full relative score with `rel_shift` and `baddbmm`.
- FireRed uses the same relative shift.
- FunASR SANM builds the full masked score.
- Granite (`granite_speech.py`) builds every block's Shaw `pos_attn` at once and fills the remainder with `-torch.finfo(dtype).max`.

### Expected behavior

#### FunASR adaptor

Attention and the FFN run on the `olens` pack. The tensor merged into the LLM is the prefix of length `fake_token_lengths`, per clip. For `L = 80`, `k = 1`: attention runs on 80 valid frames, and the merge slice is the first 10. `k` stays 1. Conv subsampling is not added to force 80 to equal 10.

`embed_multimodal` already parses `fake_token_lengths` and then ignores it. That length is threaded through. `get_encoder_outputs` keeps it. The pack is the adaptor input to `MMEncoderAttention`. `olens` is not passed as `cu_seqlens` on a rectangle.

#### Cohere and FireRed

Query chunk `C = 128`. For absolute rows `[s, e)` only:

- `ac = (q + pos_bias_u)[:, :, s:e] @ k^T` against the full key.
- `raw = (q + pos_bias_v)[:, :, s:e] @ p^T` against the full position tensor. `pos_len = query_len + key_len - 1`.
- For local row `r`, absolute `i = s + r`, and `j < key_len` only: `bd[r, j] = raw[r, (pos_len - key_len - i) + j]`. That is `raw[r, query_len - i - 1 + j]`, and it matches `rel_shift(...)[..., :key_len]`.
- `scores = scale * (ac + bd)` with `scale = 1/sqrt(d_k)` once on the sum.
- Then the existing fill, softmax, `masked_fill` of those probabilities to 0, then matmul `v`.

`rel_shift` runs on the full score, not on a chunk. Inside a chunk, `i` is the absolute row. Columns `j >= key_len` are outside this gather. The view wraps there. The shift stays an explicit gather of that form, not an `(i - j)` table.

Cohere and FireRed stay on this matmul. SDPA and flash both fail the contract: no SDPA call both scales `bd` once and zero-fills after softmax.

Cohere fill stays `-10000` on the `(i, j)` pairs `_create_masks` would mark (`regular` and `chunked_limited`, plus the query-and-key padding AND). The mask is the list of pairs, not a `(B, T, T)` allocation. A fully masked row is uniform after softmax of a constant `-10000` (`1/key_len`). The zeros come only from the following `masked_fill(..., 0)`. Filling with `-inf` and dropping that zero-fill makes the row NaN.

FireRed fill is `-inf` only where `padding_position_is_0` is 0. That is a key mask, copied onto every query row. Padded queries are not fully masked.

`rel_pos_local_attn` and `abs_pos` stay unwired. `assert calls == 1` in `test_relative_attention_fuses_score_accumulation` comes out. The numeric compare stays. `need_weights=True` concatenates the chunk probability tiles. The conformer block still uses output `[0]` only.

#### FunASR SANM

Apply `d_k ** -0.5` once. When the kernel takes `softmax_scale`, Q is left unscaled. FSMN stays after attention (`att_outs + fsmn_memory`). `mask_att_chunk_encoder` stays.

A pattern that only tightens the key mask may be a broadcast `0 / -inf` mask. A full `T×T` pattern stays on the chunked explicit masked softmax. Varlen flash is for the key-mask case.

Valid frames match the current masked matmul. A length-0 row stays finite zeros, from the post-softmax zero-fill. Pad-query rows may change under packing, because later layers key-mask them.

#### Granite

Per `context_size` block, in order: einsum that block's Shaw bias once (`pos_attn * self.scale`), SDPA with `attn_mask=pos_attn` and `scale=self.scale`, then drop `pos_attn`.

The remainder fill stays `-torch.finfo(pos_attn.dtype).max`, with `mask[:remainder, :remainder] = 0`. The fill value stays that finfo max, and the mask stays a float mask. Then `out[:, :num_features]` before `to_out`.

`SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` only if it matches per-block `MATH` on the kept rows, in fp32 and bf16, including a remainder block. Otherwise per-block MATH. `FLASH_ATTENTION` stays off. One unblocked full-sequence SDPA is a different attention pattern and is not the reference.

`input_features_mask` stays a gather on `projected_embeds` after the projector. Phi-4 `use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention` stays `True`, and that SDPA call stays as it is.

### Checks

- Cohere and FireRed: `assert_close` to the unfused reference, including a chunk whose local row 0 is not absolute row 0. A fully masked Cohere row is zeros, not NaN. A FireRed query past `input_lengths` still attends to valid keys. No score tile has query length greater than 128.
- FunASR SANM: valid frames of a padded rectangle match the current matmul. Length 0 is finite zeros. One `T×T` `mask_att_chunk_encoder` stays off varlen flash.
- FunASR adaptor: `L = 80`, `k = 1` returns 10 vectors to the LLM. The return is per clip, not `B * T_max`. Each clip's `olens` prefix matches that clip alone.
- Granite: per-block MATH matches today's blocked call on `[:, :num_features]`, with and without a remainder. The reference is that blocked call.

items.title: [Performance]: Qwen2-Audio and AudioFlamingo3 materialize a dense [B, 1, S, S] key-padding mask
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

`qwen2_audio.py` expands the padding mask to `[B, 1, S, S]` (about lines 419–426), and `audioflamingo3.py` does the same expand then `masked_fill_` (about lines 287–291). Read at `9c778e9ff8d0c78a241d7f530c441c2dc1d67533`, still present on main `e0adacc9a67a5f2b2d8ba508f7f522bc1ff83c6d` (2026-10-18).

Both masks are right-padding. Every query row is identical, so the square is a broadcast of one key mask. Visible keys stay the same. Eager adds that mask to the scores. On torch 2.5.1, the current float square, a float `[B, 1, 1, S]` `0 / -inf` mask, and a bool `[B, 1, 1, S]` with `True` = keep match with max abs diff `0`.

AudioFlamingo3's `padding_mask` True means pad. `.to(float)` puts `1.0` on pad columns and `0.0` on visible columns. `masked_fill_` writes `-inf` only on the pad. Visible keys are already `0`. This is a pad fill, not a softmax shift.

Read on transformers `v5.16.1` and `v5.19.0` (`requirements/common.txt`: `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.20.0`). `Qwen2AudioEncoder` leaves `create_bidirectional_mask` unused. `None` becomes sdpa, and sdpa forwards `[B, 1, 1, S]` without rebuilding a square.

**Proposed change.** One helper, used by Qwen2-Audio `_process_audio_input` and AudioFlamingo3 `_build_audio_encoder_attention_mask`. Each call site keeps its length math. The helper replaces the `expand` / cast / `-inf` write.

Read `self.audio_tower.config._attn_implementation` after the encoder is constructed, so a flash-to-kernel rewrite is already stored. Strip one leading `paged|`.

- `None` or `sdpa`: bool `[B, 1, 1, S]`, `True` = keep. The query axis stays 1.
- Name contains `flash` after that one strip: long `[B, S]`, `1` = valid, `0` = pad. This covers `flash_attention_2/3/4` and `kernels-community/flash-attn2`, `vllm-flash-attn3`, `aiter-flash-attn`, `flash-attn4`. A missing `flash_attn` package still counts as flash: init rewrites those names to `kernels-community/...`, and `startswith("flash_attention_")` misses them.
- `eager`: float `[B, 1, 1, S]`, `0` on visible keys and `-inf` on pad keys, dtype and device of `conv1.weight`. The bool moves to that device before `masked_fill`.
- `flex_attention` and every other name: raise, with no square allocated.
- A length-0 / all-pad row raises on the flash path. sdpa and eager still accept it (every key is pad).

Both call sites still pass the tensor as `attention_mask=`. The mask stays. `attention_mask=None` would make pad keys visible. The docstring says the mask is unused; the forward still passes it into every layer. A 4D additive mask stays off the flash path: `-inf` in the 2D `0/1` mask unpads the wrong positions.

Length grids stay:

- Qwen2-Audio width `(max_mel - 2) // 2 + 1`, row length `(input_lengths - 1) // 2 + 1`.
- AudioFlamingo3 width `(max_mel - 1) // 2 + 1`, same per-row conv length.
- `AvgPool1d(kernel=2, stride=2)` and the output-length formulas stay.

Default `None` stays sdpa. Qwen2.5-Omni, Gemma3n, and MiniCPM-O are out of scope. Qwen2.5-Omni already skips this square. Gemma3n already passes a 2D bool mask. Passing `quant_config` into either encoder is out of scope: neither constructor takes it.

### Report of performance regression

None. This is the cost of the mask as it exists on main, not a regression against an older release. Visible keys are unchanged, so model output is unchanged.

### Misc discussion on performance

The square is `B * S * S` floats per layer input for a mask whose rows are identical. The compact form is one key mask of length `S`.

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Source comparison on the commits above, plus a torch 2.5.1 check that the square, the compact float mask, and the compact bool mask match with max abs diff `0`. No full `collect_env.py` run.

### Checks

CPU only, in `tests/models/multimodal/test_audio_encoder_masks.py`. Lengths 5 and 4 with `S = 7`, plus `S = 1`.

- `None`, `sdpa`, and `paged|sdpa`: bool `[B, 1, 1, S]`, `True` iff `j < length`.
- `eager`: `0` / `-inf`, dtype and device of the arguments. Bool is moved to that device before `masked_fill`.
- Every flash name above, including one `paged|` prefix: long `[B, S]`, `1` iff `j < length`.
- `flex_attention`, `paged|paged|sdpa`, and any other name raise, with no square returned.
- A length-0 row raises on flash and is an all-`False` keep mask on sdpa.
- A successful return has the query axis at 1, or is rank-2. The last two dims are not both `S`.
- SDPA of today's square, the compact eager mask, and the compact bool mask: max abs diff `0`. AudioFlamingo3 visible entries are `0`, not `1`.

items.title: [Bug]: Ultravox syncs chunk lengths to the host, and the 3000-mel LoRA pad changes odd-length clips
items.body:
### Your current environment

Read at `9c778e9ff8d0c78a241d7f530c441c2dc1d67533`. Still present on main `e0adacc9a67a5f2b2d8ba508f7f522bc1ff83c6d` (2026-10-18): `lens_np = feature_lens.cpu().numpy()` in `vllm/model_executor/models/ultravox.py` (about line 352). The tower/connector LoRA path still pads every chunk to 3000 mel.

No `collect_env.py` output. Both failures are in the encoder forward and show up on any CUDA build.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two failures in the Ultravox audio tower.

1. **Host sync in the forward.** `_build_chunk_attn_metadata` reads `feature_lens` back to the host from both `UltravoxWhisperEncoder.forward` and `UltravoxTransformerProjector.forward`, before the layer stack. Wrapping that `.cpu().numpy()` in `gpu_sync_allowed()` leaves the stall in place.

2. **3000-mel LoRA pad changes odd-length clips.** Tower/connector LoRA pads every chunk's mel to 3000 so the punica map has a fixed width. Punica has no fixed width of 3000. Batched `Conv1d` only needs a rectangle, and `pad_and_concat_to_dim3` already zero-pads to the batch max.

   For even `L`, conv outputs already match an unpadded mel. For odd `L`, conv2's last frame reads one past `L`. Today's 3000 pad makes that tap nonzero, so every real query differs from an unpadded forward. Removing the pad without zeroing that tap first keeps the odd-`L` error.

Related, and already filed: [#61608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61608) is the punica sizing-buffer class. Ultravox is one of those models. The `mm_kwargs is None` branch below stays an upper bound so this change leaves that buffer at least as large.

### Expected behavior

`pad_audio_to_max_context` and the `F.pad` to `max_context_length` are gone. `mel <= max_context_length` stays a hard error. One tower/projector pass runs while tower or connector LoRA is on. `_MAX_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE` applies only when that LoRA is off.

1. After `gelu(conv1)`, zero conv1 time `t >= audio_lens` before conv2. That axis is the mel length, not conv2 time. The compare uses an H2D copy of the CPU `audio_lens` (`keep_on_cpu`). The CUDA length tensor stays on device for the rest of the forward.
2. Pack valid frames with a CPU index built before the tower: `feat_len = (L - 1) // 2 + 1`, flat `b * T_conv + t` for `t < feat_len[b]`. Drop zero-length rows on CPU. H2D the index, lengths, and `cu_seqlens` with `async_tensor_h2d`. The encoder has no D2H.
3. Run attention on that pack. One segment per positive chunk, length `feat_len`. `max_seqlen` stays a CPU tensor so the flash wrapper's `.item()` does not touch CUDA. Real queries attend only to real keys of the same chunk.
4. Stack each chunk with the existing `StackAudioFrames` zero-fill (at most 7 frames), then run connector linears on the packed tokens. The stack is per chunk, not on the concatenated pack. The last token stays zero-filled when `feat_len % 8 != 0`.
5. Split the packed connector output per audio under the existing post-tower `gpu_sync_allowed()`. Those `.item()` / `.tolist()` stay there. They stay out of the encoder.

`get_mm_lora_token_counts` has three calls, and each keeps its own formula.

- `mm_kwargs is None` (init sizing; `num_mm_embeds` is the encoder budget). This branch leaves `audio_lens` unread and returns the upper bound, not `(0, 0)` and not a packed sum.

  ```text
  num_chunks = ceil(num_mm_embeds / max_tokens_per_chunk)
  tower      = max(num_chunks * max_source_positions, num_mm_embeds * stack_factor)
  connector  = num_chunks * max_tokens_per_chunk
  ```

  `max_tokens_per_chunk` is `ceil(max_source_positions / stack_factor)` (188). Both tower terms are required: `B=3008` → `(24064, 3008)`; `B=8192` → `(66000, 8272)` because `8 * 8192 = 65536 < 44 * 1500 = 66000`.

- Runtime, `mm_kwargs` present and `audio_lens` missing: return `(0, 0)`. One `None` makes `set_active_mm_loras` return before the connector map is installed.

- Runtime, `audio_lens` present: that item's chunks only, in scheduler order. `tower = sum((L - 1) // 2 + 1)`, `connector = sum(ceil(feat_len / stack_factor))`. 17 mel is `(9, 2)`, not 16. Two 1-mel chunks are `(2, 2)`. The runtime tower count is that sum. It is not `num_chunks * 1500` and not `num_mm_embeds * stack_factor`.

For FlashInfer, the existing scale and batch-bucket pad use tensor ops. Batch size is `len(cu_seqlens) - 1`. Pad `sequence_lengths` with 0 out to the same bucket `add_padding_to_seqlens` uses. Pad each cumulative vector (length `batch + 1`) by repeating its last value, kept on device, so it stays length `bucket + 1`. Concatenate the Q/K section and the `* 3` V section the way `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` does. On the FP8 path both sections use `fp8_padded_hidden_size // tp_size` and neither is multiplied by 3. Bucket `max_seqlen` on the CPU integer before wrapping the 0-dim tensor. That bucket leaves which frames attend unchanged. SDPA may keep the unscaled `cu_seqlens` on CPU. Its wrapper `.tolist()` stays out of the encoder.

If a CUDA length tensor ever arrives, it stays on device. `max_seqlen` is the Python int `T_conv` from conv2's time dimension (`inputs_embeds.shape[-2]` after the permute to `[B, T, D]`), not a read of a flattened `[B * T, D]` tensor. `audio_lens` stays on CPU so that fallback is not the normal path.

The packed size comes from the CPU index built above. A CUDA `hidden[mask]` / `nonzero` is not how the packed width is learned. Linears run on the packed rows, and the reported lengths are those per-item lengths. Under LoRA there is one map and one pass.

Odd-`L` outputs will differ from today's 3000-pad forward. That difference is the point of removing the pad. Even-`L` conv outputs already match.

Ultravox stays off the Whisper CUDA-graph protocol. Packed length varies with `audio_lens`.

### Checks

- Conv: `L` in `{1, 2, 16, 17, 31, 3000}`. With the conv1 zero, every `feat_len` frame matches the unpadded conv for any right pad in `[L, 3000]`. Zeroing `t > L`, or zeroing conv2-time `t >= feat_len`, fails for odd `L`.
- Packed attention matches per-chunk SDPA on unpadded keys. An odd-`L` chunk batched with a longer chunk matches that chunk alone, and differs from today's 3000-pad forward.
- Partial stack: `feat_len` in `{1, 9, 1500}`. The last token, when `feat_len % 8 != 0`, is zero-filled and differs from today's pad-segment tail.
- LoRA stub, lengths 17 and 3000, one forward: tower rows `(9, 1500)`, connector rows `(2, 188)`, ids in item order.
- Sizing: `None` + 3008 → `(24064, 3008)`; `None` + 8192 → `(66000, 8272)`. Runtime 17 mel → `(9, 2)`. Embed-only → `(0, 0)`, and a following audio item still gets a connector map.
- A CUDA `feature_lens` whose `.cpu` raises still returns from the encoder and both projectors. The passing version has no numpy readback inside `gpu_sync_allowed`.

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3-ASR realtime flush emits the tail as a fresh ChatML prompt with no left audio
items.body:
### Your current environment

Read in `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_asr_realtime.py` at `9c778e9ff8d0c78a241d7f530c441c2dc1d67533`. Still present on main `e0adacc9a67a5f2b2d8ba508f7f522bc1ff83c6d` (2026-10-18).

No `collect_env.py` output. The failure is in how the flush prompt is built, before any GPU forward.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`read_audio` emits a fixed 5.0 s segment and leaves the remainder in the buffer. `flush` copies only that remainder. `buffer_realtime_audio` then yields it as a new ChatML `TokensPrompt` whose `multi_modal_data["audio"]` is that short slice alone.

The tower treats a zero remainder as a full chunk:

```python
chunk_lengths[tail_chunk_index] = feature_lens % (self.n_window * 2)
chunk_lengths[chunk_lengths == 0] = self.n_window * 2
```

The flush therefore starts a new window on the tail and omits the left context that chunk already covered.

Separate from this bug: text/KV carry (#56218, #51374), the language-header leak (#55786), session `prompt`/`language` (#61026), and KV reuse (#51037).

### Expected behavior

The 5.0 s gate stays as it is. Each `read_audio` segment stays exactly `segment_size` samples. After a segment is returned, the buffer remembers only that segment's last tower chunk and prepends it once on the next non-empty flush.

```text
chunk_frames = n_window * 2          # loaded audio_config.n_window
rem_frames   = feature_lens % chunk_frames
if rem_frames == 0:
    rem_frames = chunk_frames
carry_samples = rem_frames * hop_length
```

`hop_length` and `feature_lens` come from the loaded feature extractor, on that hop grid. The carry is the trailing `carry_samples` of the segment just yielded.

A 5.0 s segment is 80000 samples. Hop 160 makes 500 mel frames.

- Checkpoint `n_window=50` (`chunk_frames=100`): `500 % 100 == 0`, so the last chunk is 100 frames. Carry = 16000 samples.
- In-tree default `n_window=100` (`chunk_frames=200`): `500 % 200 == 100`. Carry is also 16000 samples. The last chunk starts at frame 400. A fixed `2 * n_window * hop` prefix is 32000 samples and starts at frame 300, inside the finished chunk.

Rules that follow from the tower:

- A stream that never filled one segment has an empty carry. `flush` returns the tail unchanged.
- `flush` of an empty buffer stays `None`. A held carry is not a prompt by itself.
- A non-empty `flush` returns `concat(carry, tail)` once, then clears the carry. A second `flush` is `None`.
- Later `read_audio` segments stay exactly `segment_size`. The client already appends deltas, so the carry belongs on the flush only.
- The carry width is `rem_frames * hop_length` from the loaded `n_window`. `n_window_infer` is a different field.
- The ChatML `prompt_token_ids` stay the same template. The extra audio is only in `multi_modal_data["audio"]`.

The token delta is whatever `_get_feat_extract_output_lengths` returns for the flush mel length minus the tail-only mel length. `+13` happens only when those two mel lengths differ by 100. Mel length is the extractor's attention-mask sum, not `len(samples) / hop`.

- `Qwen3ASRFeatureExtractor` (`min_length=8000`, pad counted in the mask): 1600 samples can be 50 frames / 7 tokens, and 17600 samples can be 110 frames / 15 tokens. Delta `+8`.
- `WhisperFeatureExtractor` (what Qwen/Qwen3-ASR ships; no `min_length`): `+13` only after the two measured mask sums differ by 100.

Official `finish_streaming_transcribe` re-decodes the whole waveform. This change leaves that path alone. Conv outputs at the junction will differ from that re-decode. There is no text-prefix rollback.

Out of scope: the 5.0 s gate, reading `input_stream`, and echo cancellation.

### Checks

Buffer only, no weights. `sampling_rate=16000`, hop 160.

- Under 80000 samples: `read_audio` is `None`. `flush` equals those samples.
- Exactly 80000: one `read_audio` of 80000. `flush` is `None` even though a carry was saved.
- 80000 + 1600, both `n_window=50` and `n_window=100`: `read_audio` is the first 80000 unchanged. `flush` has length 17600 and starts with `segment[-16000:]`. A 32000-sample prefix fails this check.
- Two full segments plus a tail: the carry is the end of the second segment only.
- A second `flush` after a non-empty flush is `None`.
- Token check uses the real extractor. `Qwen3ASRFeatureExtractor`: 1600 vs 17600 can be 7 and 15 tokens (`+8`). `WhisperFeatureExtractor`: `+13` only when the measured mel lengths differ by 100.

items.title: [Performance]:Skip gaps in sliding-window prefix-cache hit search
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance


`SlidingWindowManager.find_longest_cache_hit` currently scans every block from right to left, costing up to `max_num_blocks` `BlockPool.get_cached_block` lookups even when the cache is cold. Sliding-window groups commonly run at a low hit rate, so a 128K-token request with a 4K window performs ~8192 lookups (block_size=16) although a hit only needs `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) = 256` contiguous blocks. The function already carries a TODO for this. Proposed change: probe every `stride = sliding_window_contiguous_blocks`-th block from the right. Every candidate run of `stride` cached blocks contains exactly one probe, so the lattice cannot skip a hit. On a probe hit, expand to the right (at most `stride - 1` blocks, since the next probe missed), verify only windows containing the probe, and after a miss at `idx` resume at the next aligned edge below `idx - 1`. Alignment retries advance by `alignment_tokens // gcd(alignment_tokens, block_size)` blocks, and the cached-prefix fallback is computed directly. Function-level measurements (`find_longest_cache_hit`, block_size=16, sliding_window=4096, 128K tokens, alignment=16, no EAGLE, single-thread CPU):

| pattern | main lookups | proposed lookups | main time | proposed time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cold cache | 8192 | 33 | 4.49 ms | 0.021 ms |
| 1% random cached | 8192 | 33 | 4.61 ms | 0.021 ms |
| tail hit / full cache | 256 | 257 | 0.23 ms | 0.23 ms |
| adversary (cached blocks on the probe lattice) | 8192 | 128 | 4.63 ms | 0.11 ms |

The worst case remains O(max_num_blocks), but the common low-hit-rate case becomes O(max_num_blocks / stride), and the measured adversarial case is still well below the current full scan.



### Report of performance regression

_No response_

### Misc discussion on performance

### Relation to #53276 (not a duplicate)

#53276 targets the same TODO with a different, narrower approach: it checks `block_hashes[i - K + 1]` only when the current block misses and no run is being accumulated, and jumps by K only in that case. Every other path still advances one block at a time, alignment retries remain per-block, the cached-prefix fallback still comes from the full scan, and the PR adds no tests. This proposal is materially different:
- Every probe hit triggers right-expansion and verification bounded to windows containing the probe, so gaps are skipped regardless of which side the miss is on.
- Alignment retries jump by the alignment period, covering hybrid models where `alignment_tokens != block_size`.
- The cached-prefix fallback is computed directly.
- Correctness is backed by an offline exhaustive comparison with the previous implementation (all cached-block patterns up to 13 blocks over a grid of block sizes, windows, alignments, and EAGLE settings: 7,339,584 cases, 0 differences) plus a committed randomized test.

Happy to close this in favor of #53276 if maintainers prefer that direction.

  ### Additional robustness fix

`sliding_window=1` with EAGLE disabled makes `_contiguous_blocks_for_hit` return 0, which would leave the new probe loop's `i -= stride` at the same index. The implementation clamps the stride to 1, reproducing the previous behavior (one cached block is reusable) and terminating; a regression test is included.

  ### Misc discussion on performance

This is a scheduler-side CPU optimization; it does not change hit results, model output, or GPU execution. End-to-end serving numbers have not been collected yet.


### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0+cu132, upstream main at ff01a6b14f, CPU unit-test harness. This is a scheduler-side CPU optimization and does not change hit results, model output, or GPU execution.

The LoRA branch ([model.py#L724-L727](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py#L724-L727)) rebinds `self.packed_modules_mapping` on the instance, but the quant config keeps the class dict from step 2. That is why `--enable-lora` does not avoid the error, although the indexer is not fused in that mode. ModelOpt FP4 is already special-cased with `without_modelopt_fp4`. Other formats are not. Changing the checkpoint's `ignore` list does not help. It describes how the weights are stored (q/k/v packed INT4, `index_qk_proj` BF16). The fourth shard comes from vLLM's `packed_modules_mapping`, not from the checkpoint. ### Scope We read `model.safetensors.index.json` of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next quantized checkpoints on the Hub (2026-10-18). In 26 of the 82 quantized (non-GGUF, non-MLX) checkpoints we could inspect, layer 3 `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` carry quantization tensors and `index_qk_proj` has only `.weight`. Examples with compressed-tensors and the indexer in `ignore`: - `davetha/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DERISKED-W4A16-AWQ` - `VnimanieAI/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16` - `primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-mixed-NVFP4-FP8` - `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ` `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` and `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` leave attention unquantized and are not affected. ### Workaround we use A runtime patch sets `packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` to `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` on both model classes and turns `fuse_indexer_projection` off. With it, the Swift checkpoint loads on 4x A100-40GB (TP4 + EP) and passes our functional and speed smoke tests. The indexer then runs as its own GEMM, as before #59533. ### Proposed fix Fuse the indexer into `qkv_proj` only when `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and `index_qk_proj` resolve to the same quantization. Otherwise keep the indexer as its own layer, and give the quant config a packed mapping that matches that decision (per model instance, not the class dict). This also fixes the `--enable-lora` path. I would like to send a PR for this. @gau-nernst, does this direction fit #59533, or do you prefer another approach? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug If a `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses` request carries `kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids`, the renderer feeds those ids to the engine in place of the rendered `messages`, which skips the chat template, `truncate_prompt_tokens` and tokenization. This decode-side reuse is meant for disaggregated prefill and decode with a KV connector (`docs/features/disagg_prefill.md` limits it to `/v1/chat/completions` with a connector configured), but nothing checks that a connector is configured or which endpoint the request came in on, so it works on every server. A client can send harmless `messages` while the model runs on a prompt of its choosing, with the chat template and any system prompt it carries removed. Raised with the security team first, who asked for it as a regular issue: only the requester's own response is affected and `/v1/completions` already accepts raw token ids. First affected release: 0.27.0, which added the reuse path in #48145. Reproduced on 0.31.0. On `main` (371745ebd) #55771 and #59555 added shape and vocabulary checks, but there is still no check for a KV connector or for the endpoint. **Reproduction** (no GPU needed; builds the same `OnlineRenderer` the API server uses, with no KV transfer config, and renders one chat request with and without `kv_transfer_params`): ```python import asyncio import vllm from vllm.config import DeviceConfig, ModelConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest from vllm.renderers import renderer_from_config from vllm.renderers.online_renderer import OnlineRenderer print("vllm", vllm.__version__) config = VllmConfig(model_config=ModelConfig(model="Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct"), device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cpu")) print("kv_transfer_config:", config.kv_transfer_config) # no KV connector renderer = renderer_from_config(config) online = OnlineRenderer( model_config=config.model_config, renderer=renderer, request_logger=None, chat_template=None, chat_template_content_format="auto", ) messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}] async def render(body): conversation, (engine_input,) = await online.render_chat( ChatCompletionRequest(**body)) return conversation, engine_input["prompt_token_ids"] base = {"model": "Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct", "messages": messages} conv, ids = asyncio.run(render(base)) print("plain request: conversation:", len(conv), "messages; engine ids:", ids) conv, ids = asyncio.run(render( {**base, "kv_transfer_params": {"prompt_token_ids": [10, 20, 30]}})) print("with kv params: conversation:", len(conv), "messages; engine ids:", ids) print("tokenizer.decode(engine ids):", repr(renderer.tokenizer.decode(ids))) ``` Output on 0.31.0: ``` vllm 0.31.0 kv_transfer_config: None plain request: conversation: 1 messages; engine ids: [151644, 8948, 198, 2610, 525, 264, 10950, 17847, 13, 151645, 198, 151644, 872, 198, 3838, 374, 279, 6722, 315, 9625, 30, 151645, 198, 151644, 77091, 198] with kv params: conversation: 0 messages; engine ids: [10, 20, 30] tokenizer.decode(engine ids): '+5?' ``` With no connector configured, the same `messages` render to the templated prompt (system prompt included) in the first case; in the second the engine gets exactly the client's three ids and the conversation is empty. The same branch is reached from `/v1/responses` through `render_responses`. **Where** (`main` at 371745ebd): - `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py` lines 106-150: `_reused_prompt_token_ids` pops `kv_transfer_params["prompt_token_ids"]` from any request and checks only that the ids are a non-empty list of valid token ids. - `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py` lines 794-802: `preprocess_chat` builds `tokens_input(reuse_ids, ...)` and skips `render_chat_async`, so the template and `tok_params` are never applied. The Harmony chat path does the same at lines 543-547. - `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py` line 373: `render_responses` calls the same `preprocess_chat`, and `ResponsesRequest` declares `kv_transfer_params`. - `vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py` lines 154 and 280: `has_kv_connector` is set and read only for the transfer cleanup, never for the reuse decision. **Suggested fix**: pass the connector state into the renderer and honour `kv_transfer_params["prompt_token_ids"]` only when a KV connector is configured and the endpoint is `/v1/chat/completions`, as documented. items.title: [Feature][KV Offload]: Require canonical_layout when a secondary tier shares KV across TP sizes (direct layout silently corrupts)
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Requirement:** when the `OffloadingConnector` is configured with a secondary tier whose storage namespace is shared across parallel layouts (`fs`, `obj`, `p2p`), check at startup that `canonical_layout` is enabled. If it isn't, fail with a clear error (or fall back to a topology-specific namespace) instead of silently loading KV that was written under a different TP size.

**Why:** today `canonical_layout` defaults to `false`, and a deployment can share a secondary tier between engines with different TP sizes without any warning. In one case the engine loads the other engine's direct-layout blocks and returns corrupted output.

The direct-layout `is_parallelism_agnostic` gate (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`, around line 179) holds for a single head-sharded full-attention group on the V1 model runner. When it holds, the FS/OBJ/P2P managers build their namespace with `parallel_agnostic=True` (`file_mapper.py`), so TP is removed from the namespace hash. A direct-layout CPU chunk is laid out as each worker's page side by side (`|W0|W1|...`), not as head-interleaved per-layer data. The same block hash therefore maps to bytes that mean different things under different TP sizes.

**Reproduction** (4×H200, nightly 0.32.0rc1.dev100, Llama-3.2-1B, gsm8k via `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/run_accuracy_test.sh` from #61846):

| Setup | Model runner | `canonical_layout` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P2P, TP1 prefiller → TP2 decoder | V2 (default) | false | config fingerprint mismatch, 0 tokens transferred, recompute (safe) |
| P2P, TP1 → TP2 | V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | false | all tokens transferred, **accuracy 0.0, gibberish** |
| FS tier, TP1 writes → TP2 reads, same `root_dir` | V1 | false | 3072 hits, same namespace hash, **0/4 outputs match** |
| FS tier, TP1 → TP1 (control) | V1 | false | correct |
| P2P, TP1 ↔ TP2, both directions | V1 and V2 | **true** | correct (0.340 / 0.343, baseline 0.332), 5120/5120 tokens |
| P2P MLA (DeepSeek-V2-Lite), TP1 ↔ TP2 | V1 and V2 | **true** | correct (0.656 / 0.661) |

The corruption needs all of the following: the direct layout, the V1 model runner, a model that passes the direct-layout agnostic gate, and two engines with different TP sizes sharing one secondary tier. Nothing in the config or logs tells the user they're in that state. The usage guide also didn't document `canonical_layout` until #61822.

**Proposed behavior** (open for discussion):

1. At config build time, if `secondary_tiers` contains a tier that uses the parallel-agnostic namespace and `canonical_layout` is false, either:
   - raise a `ValueError` asking the user to set `"canonical_layout": true`, or
   - never treat direct-layout bytes as parallelism-agnostic, so the namespace keeps TP and cross-TP reads miss instead of corrupt. #55191 does this for the FS tier; it would need to apply to OBJ/P2P too. Then log a warning that cross-TP sharing needs `canonical_layout`.
2. Add a test that the misconfiguration is rejected (or kept in a separate namespace) before any KV is loaded, plus an e2e direct-layout mixed-TP guard asserting no corrupted reuse. #61846 already has an `EXPECT_TRANSFER=0` check for the P2P tier.

### Alternatives

- **Turn `canonical_layout` on by default whenever a secondary tier is configured.** This removes the footgun but changes the copy path and on-disk format for existing same-TP deployments, and fails at startup for models the canonical mapping can't certify yet.
- **Documentation only (#61822).** Necessary, but users who never read it can still hit silent corruption.

### Additional context

- Tracking issue: #61886 (TP-agnostic KV offloading). This would fit under "Correctness and cache identity" next to #55191.
- Related: #55191 (topology-specific direct caches, FS), #55904 (namespace not keyed by KV cache layout), #61846 (P2P e2e matrix, mixed-TP configs run with `canonical_layout`).
- AI assistance was used to write this issue. The reproduction results come from runs I did on the hardware above.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Problem.** With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` and `--enable-sleep-mode`, a start with empty compile caches (first start after install or upgrade) of the command below fails while allocating the KV cache (`allocate_kv_cache`, `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`):

```text
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4.46 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.82 GiB of which 946.25 MiB is free. Of the allocated memory 26.80 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 4.76 GiB allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 2.35 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.
```

With warm caches the same command started in our tests, so the failure looks intermittent. Seen with both `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and `nvfp4`. The model's weights are NVFP4, which is where the buffer below comes from; other weight formats were not tested, but the missing guards are not format-specific. v0.31.0 also lacks both in this branch (not run).

**Cause.** The `kv_cache_memory_bytes` branch of `Worker.determine_available_memory()` runs `profile_run()` without either allocator guard that the memory-profiling branch has:

1. **No cache release.** `memory_profiling` runs `gc.collect()` and `empty_cache()` on exit; this branch does not, so fully free cached segments (2.4 GiB here) stay reserved. The open PR #59893 adds this release.
2. **No split limit.** #58430 runs the memory-profiling `profile_run()` inside `_scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20)`; this branch does not. A snapshot just before KV allocation (both instrumented unpatched cold starts) showed a 2,426 MiB segment kept reserved by a single live 40 MiB FlashInfer scratch buffer (`flashinfer/utils.py` `_get_cache_buf`, from `mm_fp4`). `empty_cache()` cannot release that segment while the scratch buffer remains live; with #59893 alone, device-free memory also stayed lower after start-up and after a 10,408-token request.

With sleep mode the KV cache is allocated in the separate CuMem pool, so these retained default-pool reservations reduce the device memory available to it. `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` also sets `kv_cache_memory_bytes` (from a saved plan), so those starts take the same branch.

**Fix.** #59893 plus the split limit on the same `profile_run()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`, on top of #59893):

```diff
         if kv_cache_memory_bytes := self.cache_config.kv_cache_memory_bytes:
             # still need a profile run which compiles the model for
             # max_num_batched_tokens
-            with set_current_vllm_config(self.vllm_config):
+            # Same allocator split limit as the memory-profiling branch below.
+            with (
+                self._scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20),
+                set_current_vllm_config(self.vllm_config),
+            ):
                 self.model_runner.profile_run(
                     randomize_inputs=self.randomize_dummy_inputs
                 )
```

#59893's test then needs the real scope on its stand-in worker (one statement, in the suggestion on that PR). With both, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` passes on main `1b2a666` (26 tests, including #59893's GPU test), and so do vLLM's pre-commit hooks. The suggested source and test changes are posted on #59893; this report does not propose a separate PR.

**Verification** (vLLM nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev35+g656d0d450`). `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, 4.5 GiB KV budget, sleep mode. All rows used empty vLLM, inductor and Triton cache folders; in the last two rows, every start also completed a short request and a 10,408-token prompt:

| | KV dtype | Starts | Free before KV allocation | Free after the 10K request | Engine init | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unpatched | fp8 / nvfp4 | 3 / 1 | 3.49 GiB (2 measured) | - | - | OOM every time |
| Split limit only | fp8 / nvfp4 | 3 / 2 | 4.59 to 4.66 GiB | - | - | Starts |
| #59893 only | fp8 / nvfp4 | 2 / 2 | 5.79 to 5.81 GiB | 1.02 to 1.09 GiB | 94.2 to 107.6 s | Starts, serves |
| #59893 + split limit | fp8 / nvfp4 | 1 / 1 | 8.64 GiB | 2.15 to 2.27 GiB | 73.8 to 74.4 s | Starts, serves |

The last two rows were measured on the same day, with about 0.81 GiB of other GPU usage before start-up; engine-init times are as observed, not explained. The same code with a different comment wording also started 5 of 5 cold starts (fp8 2, nvfp4 3) with 8.64 GiB free before KV allocation. The open PR #56698 also avoided this OOM in our tests: it removes this branch, so pinned sizes are profiled and checked against an estimate; it targets a different failure (a pin too large for the activation peak).

Related but distinct: #54122 and #54209 concern cold-compilation peaks inflating activation estimates on the `--gpu-memory-utilization` path. The pinned path skips that sizing calculation, and #54209 resets peak counters without releasing cached memory or preventing live scratch buffers from pinning segments.

Workaround until fixed: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:20` (CUDA graph memory rose from 0.25 to 2.42 GiB here).

**Reproduce.**

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/cold/vllm /tmp/cold/inductor /tmp/cold/triton
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/cold/vllm TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/cold/inductor TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/cold/triton \
vllm serve unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 98304 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4831838208 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --enable-sleep-mode --language-model-only --max-num-seqs 2
```

Use new empty folders for each attempt; with warm caches it started in our tests.

Background: found while testing NVFP4 KV cache on SM120 (#46963, #60452). On v0.30.0, FP8 was the smallest KV cache type on this GPU; NVFP4 fits 54% to 57% more tokens in the same budget (Qwen3.8-27B: 109,794 to 169,082; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 157,640 to 248,200).

Repro, which is the command from `docs/design/attention_backends.md`:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --attention-backend b12x
```

or offline:

from vllm import LLM
LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", attention_config={"backend": "B12X"})

Cause: `B12xPagedAttentionImpl.__init__` checks `cache_config.block_size` against `(64, 128)`. The check is also redundant: a user-specified unsupported size is already rejected at backend selection via `supports_block_size()`, and the runtime page size comes from the KV cache tensors. The existing tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py` pass `block_size=64/128` explicitly, so they never hit this.

Workaround: pass `--block-size 64` or `--block-size 128`.

items.title: [Feature] Support box and ground decision primitives with GUI-Actor pointer-head models
items.body:
# [Feature] Support `box` and `ground` decision primitives with GUI-Actor pointer-head models

## Motivation

The structured decisions API (`/v1/systemone`) answers questions about a state by
scoring a fixed set of options: `choice`, `noul`, `score`. That covers
classification and routing, but not what is often the next question about the
same input — **where** something is in an attached image.

GUI grounding models answer exactly that, and they do not do it by generating
text: a pointer head scores the image's visual patches against a query hidden
state and the answer is read off that distribution. There is no way to express
such a question through the current API, and no vLLM architecture serves these
checkpoints.

## Proposed API

Two new question types on `/v1/systemone`, matching the "System One" contract
(the reference serving layer's request shape):

```jsonc
{
  "state": "a screenshot of a checkout page",
  "images": ["https://example.com/shot.png"],
  "questions": {
    "pay":  {"type": "box",    "instructions": "the Pay button"},
    "cart": {"type": "ground", "instructions": "the cart icon"}
  }
}
```

| type | criteria | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `box` | `null`; the question needs one image | `box` (`left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` as fractions of the image), `confidence` |
| `ground` | `null`; the question needs one image | `point` (`[x, y]` in 0–999), `confidence`, `topk_points` |

Neither carries `probabilities` — a spatial answer is a region, not a
distribution over options. `confidence` is the probability mass the predicted
region holds.

## Design notes worth reviewing

- **Pooler output is the raw patch distribution**, not a softmax. The decode
  applies the checkpoint's fitted temperature to the confidence afterwards, and
  a second softmax over an already-normalised row would move the geometry.
- **Chunked prefill and prefix caching must be off** for such a model: the
  answer is read from the image patches of the prompt's own prefill.
- **The model is identified by its weights** (`multi_patch_pointer_head.`
  tensors), not by a config field — a config can claim the pointer token ids
  without a trained head.
- **A question type a model cannot answer returns 501**, not 400, since a
  different model would accept the same request.

## Scope

- Serving `microsoft/GUI-Actor-{3B,7B}-Qwen2.5-VL` (Qwen2.5-VL backbones).
  Qwen3-VL / Qwen3.5 would be follow-ups.
- `/v1/decisions` keeps OpenAI's schema and does not gain these types.

## Implementation

Opening this issue to get a design read on the API surface before submitting an
implementation — in particular whether `box` / `ground` should be first-class question types
alongside `choice` / `noul` / `score`, and whether the reference-compatible
answer shape (edges as fractions, points as 0–999 integers) is the right one for
vLLM rather than, say, pixel coordinates.

For the host group, `_request_remaining_blocks` (3149) gets 0 back from `get_num_blocks_to_allocate(..., apply_admission_cap=True)` as long as A1's remaining host pages fit the current free count. So A2 is admitted against host blocks A1 still needs. - `scheduler.py:969-971` always drains `kv_holding_waiting` first, oldest first (`skip_request` at 959-965 and `prepend_requests` at 1462). At 1330-1336, `if new_blocks is None: ... break` ends the pass on A1. Waiting requests are never preempted. - The test added with #59036, `test_hisparse_admitted_async_loads_can_finish_with_nothing_running` in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`, uses 3 usable host blocks and two 3-page prompts. Only one load is ever admitted there, so the two-admitted case is not covered. This is in 0.31.0 through the cherry-pick of #59036 and is unchanged on main. Proposed fix: at async admission, subtract the remaining host pages of the requests in `_inflight_prefills` from the host free count, the way the GPU side reserves for in-flight loads. Alternatively, let the `kv_holding_waiting` pass skip past a host-capacity failure instead of breaking. A regression test with the shape above (pool of 6, prompts of 4 and 3 pages, 2 matched pages each, both loads finished) fails today. I can open a PR for this. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: sharded_state can't round-trip models with attention/KV-cache scale params (Missing keys ...attn.q_scale, k_scale, v_scale, prob_scale)
items.body:
### Your current environment

- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` (digest `c1c9f6fd5c10…`), torch 2.13.0+cu130
- 2x NVIDIA H20 (SM90), TP=2
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` (block-FP8)
- The relevant code is unchanged on main (`08a65e2`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Saving a `sharded_state` checkpoint and loading it back with **identical** settings fails for any model whose attention layers use `BaseKVCacheMethod` (FP8 checkpoints and the like):

```
ValueError: Missing keys ('language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.q_scale',
 'language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.k_scale', 'language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.v_scale',
 'language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.attn.prob_scale', ...) in loaded state!
```

**Repro**

```bash
python examples/features/sharded_state/save_sharded_state_offline.py \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enforce-eager --output /tmp/q38_sharded
vllm serve /tmp/q38_sharded --load-format sharded_state --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192
```

**Cause**

1. `BaseKVCacheMethod.create_weights` registers placeholder parameters `q_scale`, `k_scale`, `v_scale` and `prob_scale` (initialized to -1.0).
2. `process_weights_after_loading` copies their values into the `_q_scale` / `_k_scale` / ... buffers and then `del`s the placeholders.
3. `save_sharded_state` runs on the fully loaded engine, so the shards contain only `attn._k_scale`, `_v_scale`, `_q_scale` and `_prob_scale`. I checked the saved files: each rank has the 4 `_*_scale` buffers for each of the 16 full-attention layers (64 keys), and no `k_scale`.
4. `ShardedStateLoader.load_weights` iterates over a freshly created model, which still has the placeholders. They are never loaded, so it raises `Missing keys`.

The existing round-trip test only uses `Llama-3.2-1B` in BF16, which has no such placeholders. That is why this hasn't shown up.

**Patching the keys in is not a real fix.** Adding the keys with -1.0 makes it load. But then `process_weights_after_loading` runs a second time on already-processed weights (`base_loader.load_model` always calls it). It sees `k_scale = -1` and overwrites the loaded `_k_scale` with 1.0, so a checkpoint with calibrated KV scales would silently lose them. For this checkpoint (no calibrated scales) the patched round trip did give correct output.

**Suggested fix**

A `sharded_state` checkpoint holds post-processed weights, the same as the weight-cache IPC loader from #54921 ("Fast Start"). That PR already added `weights_already_processed()` / `supports_pre_processed_weights`. Under that mode, `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading` drops the placeholders and rebuilds `_*_scale_float` / `_*_scale_cpu` from the loaded buffers.

So I think `ShardedStateLoader` should:

- load and post-process under `weights_already_processed()`;
- not require keys that only exist as pre-processing placeholders.

One trade-off: quant methods that don't declare `supports_pre_processed_weights` would then raise in `process_weights_after_loading` instead of being processed twice. That seems more correct, but it changes behavior for methods that happen to tolerate double processing today.

Would maintainers prefer that approach, or something narrower? I'm happy to send the PR.

Related: #62155 (`ShardedStateLoader` silently partially loads shape-mismatched tensors; root cause of #61681), found during the same investigation.
